CHIEF COMPLAINT
Post-operative follow-up status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 36-year-old female presenting for follow-up after bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on 10/10/2020. She reports her breasts are doing well. Denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. She reports resolution of back pain. During previous visit with PA Ruth Sanchez in March, a lump was noted under the left breast; patient has not palpated this since and has been performing self-massage. Patient reports the surgical scars have been bothersome, particularly one incision, and has been using Mederma scar gel daily. She is otherwise doing well and reports enjoying summertime.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative for chills, fever, nausea, vomiting, and back pain. All other systems reviewed and unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty (10/10/2020)

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel - applied daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in visit

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is enjoying summertime. Family doing well.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Breasts: Bilateral incisions well-healed with no signs of infection or erythema. Some widening of scars noted, particularly on the left breast. No lumps palpated. No concerning findings on examination.

RESULTS
Photography to be obtained today for documentation and future comparison.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty with appropriate healing. Continue Mederma scar gel twice daily with massage to improve scar appearance and texture. Discussed that scar revision will not be performed until at least one year post-operatively due to high tissue tension. Follow-up appointment scheduled in 6 months to reassess scars and discuss possible revision at that time. Obtain photographs today for future comparison.
